prompts.name: rust-async-cancellation-editorial
prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: premium editorial cover for Crabrix's Rust engineering blog, wide landscape 3:2, 1536x1024. Topic: asynchronous cancellation, preserving ownership and work. Create a striking tactile isometric cut-paper and refined 3D editorial scene, dark midnight navy background, warm ivory, coral-orange and jade with delicate brass detail. A small expressive orange crab engineer carefully holds a sealed ivory job envelope at a brass dispatch console, while a bounded queue of exactly three ivory slots sits on the right. A round timer with a coral rim sits separately at the back; a slim jade route to the queue remains intact, a coral route curves back to the crab. This is a conceptual illustration, not a scientific chart: no numbers, no arrows implying rollback, no text, no fake code, no logos or watermarks. Sophisticated lighting, generous breathing room, crisp edges and focal hierarchy, beautiful enough for a technical magazine. Crab must have a clearly readable shell, two claws and small legs. No game or existing commercial character references.

prompts.name: rust-async-cancellation-ownership-infographic
prompts.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: technically accurate Rust cancellation infographic, wide landscape 3:2, 1536x1024. Premium dark navy editorial design matching an engineering magazine: warm ivory typography, jade success routes, coral cancellation route, restrained brass details, clear readable sans serif. Title exactly: "Reserve first. Move second." Subtitle exactly: "A timeout before reservation keeps the job with the caller." Show a clean large left-to-right ownership diagram with 3 main boxes labelled exactly "Caller owns job", "Await capacity", "Permit acquired". Solid jade arrows connect these boxes in that order. From "Permit acquired" a final jade arrow reaches a right-side box labelled "Send without await" with a small bounded queue icon. A separate coral branch goes downward ONLY from "Await capacity" to a bottom-left box labelled "Timeout: return job". Under the final box small note exactly "Enqueued does not mean processed". Under timeout box small note exactly "No job moved into send future". A tiny orange crab at the original caller holding an ivory envelope; repeated envelope icon is allowed to illustrate ownership transfer but never suggest duplicate jobs. Avoid any arrow returning from the enqueued state to the caller; do not depict rollback. Do not include source code, performance statistics, extra labels, decorative dense microtext, logos or watermarks. Keep diagram substantially larger than decoration, immaculate spacing and arrow routing.

prompts.name: rust-async-cancellation-deadline-infographic
prompts.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: analytical illustration for an article on Tokio cancellation, wide landscape 3:2, 1536x1024. Premium technical editorial graphic on midnight navy with warm ivory text, jade task tracks, coral deadline, fine brass separators. Title exactly "A timeout stops waiting". Subtitle exactly "It does not undo a side effect." Show two clean horizontal conceptual timelines, no numerical scale and no performance claims. Upper row label exactly "Direct future"; a jade capsule labelled "Work" begins left and stops at a central vertical coral dashed line labelled "Deadline". To its right an ivory note exactly "Future dropped" and a second note exactly "Earlier effects may remain". Lower row label exactly "Spawned task"; a jade task track continues visibly beyond the same deadline line to the right. Beside that continuation, label exactly "Dropping JoinHandle detaches". Under both timelines, a visually separated footnote exactly "Keep the handle. Request shutdown. Await completion." A small orange crab engineer watches the lower continuing task from the lower left, subordinate to the explanatory tracks. Make clear the spawned task is separate from its waiting handle. Do not show the spawned task being killed by the deadline. Do not add clocks with measured seconds, charts with fabricated values, source code, commercial logos or watermarks. Elegant editorial hierarchy and flawless legibility.
